authority: User $implement docs/features/core-workbench request; approved bundle 64bcf577a30e7c6bbff3e4e775f8e6c17ca212ce3bf79b5bc5be31196a792b07; approved PLAN p2.6 CW-13; formally passed CW-10/CW-11/CW-12 dependencies
objective: Implement the bounded Manager recovery, termination, and second-level completion-decision policy for C-AC-04/07/10/13/31/34.
dependency_contracts: Consume CW-10 immutable TaskSpec/revision/run identity and confirmed terminal lifecycle facts; do not weaken repository authority or terminal ownership.
Consume CW-11 worker judgment sources, criteria, evidence errors and unknowns as first-level evidence; exit code 0 alone is never success.
Consume CW-12 automation/pause/cancel/revocation state as a hard gate on new automatic analysis, mutation, worker instruction, relaunch, or forced termination.
required_behavior: Provide typed, fail-closed policy records and a small coordinator/port boundary under one new recovery_* package; keep policy deterministic and fixture-testable.

Bind every decision to exact task/revision/run, approved completion criteria, worker evidence provenance, current authority/scope, retry usage and current session settings revision. Reject identity mismatches and malformed or incomplete evidence.

Second-level outcomes must distinguish confirmed completion, confirmed failure, additional investigation, bounded recovery retry, blocked/unresolved report, and termination steps. Preserve sources, evidence, attempts, unknowns and remaining problems in the report.

Recovery retries are task-wide, default maximum three, exclude initial execution and normal improvement, never reset on commit/name/revision/session-setting changes, and stop automatically before a fourth recovery. Do not impose an elapsed-time experiment limit.
Require confirmed full termination before source/config mutation, new worker instruction, or relaunch. A stop request, main-process exit, or unknown lifetime is insufficient.

New TaskSpec revisions apply to the next run by default. A current-run apply request must request stop and wait for confirmed termination before mutation/relaunch. Immediate stop or authority revocation applies to the current run without waiting for the next revision.
Session settings changes apply to subsequent decisions, do not terminate the current run, and preserve retry usage.

Forced termination is allowed only when explicitly delegated and the exact owned target identity is confirmed; otherwise return a confirmation-required/blocked result. After force action, require a fresh observation proving full termination before mutation/relaunch.
Never bypass terminal input owner, replay an uncertain command, or treat pause/resume/restart as authority.
verification_matrix: success log/result with exit 0; nonzero failure; exit 0 criteria failure; missing/changed log or result; unknown termination
retry attempts one through three and fourth blocked; retry count retained across new commit, revision and settings changes; initial and normal improvement excluded
termination-before-mutation/relaunch, stop request without exit, main exit with descendants/return barrier unknown, no elapsed-time cutoff
next-run revision default, current-run apply stop-confirm-mutate-relaunch, immediate revocation
forced termination delegated/undelegated, exact/ambiguous/wrong target, post-force exit unknown/confirmed
pause/cancel/revocation/metadata failure gates, user terminal owner preserved, and evidence-rich unresolved reports
constraints: Sole writer; preserve unrelated dirty changes and do not modify existing CW-10/CW-11/CW-12 production modules.
Use apply_patch; Python/Linux only; no new dependency, Phase 2, multiplexer dependency, Docker, delegation, commit, publish, or deploy.
Run focused fixture tests, all tests in the new recovery package, relevant predecessor regressions, and graphify update .
report: Return changed paths, public contracts and invariants, exact checks/counts, acceptance mapping, candidate_ready/blocker, and residual integration risks for CW-15.
